card.lives_in: Bletchley, Milton Keynes, South East England
card.occupation: Injection moulding machine operator at a plastics packaging plant on an industrial estate in Milton Keynes. He works a rotating four-on, four-off shift pattern, around 42 hours a week averaged out.
card.education_detail: Finished secondary school in Lithuania, then did a two-year vocational course in mechanics and equipment maintenance at a technical school in Panevėžys. In the UK he has done a forklift licence (counterbalance and reach) and in-house training on machine changeovers and basic health and safety. He has no UK qualifications beyond those.
card.household: Lives alone in a rented one-bedroom flat above a row of shops in Bletchley. Never married. He had a long relationship in his late twenties that ended about seven years ago. No children. Pays the rent on time every month and keeps the place very tidy.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in a small town near Panevėžys, Lithuania. He moved to the UK in 2008 at 22, first doing agency work in a Northampton warehouse, then moved to Milton Keynes for steadier factory work. Raised Catholic. He still calls himself Christian and goes to the Lithuanian or Polish mass at Christmas and Easter, but not week to week. He speaks Lithuanian with his mother on video calls every Sunday. He has settled status and has thought about applying for citizenship, mostly for practical reasons.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and precise. He is usually first on the line, checks his machine settings himself and keeps his station clean. He gets irritated by colleagues who are slow or careless and says so, which doesn't make him popular, but supervisors trust him with changeovers. He knows how to work the overtime system to his advantage and will happily take the best-paid shifts before anyone else hears about them. He isn't interested in team-building or social events at work.
card.sports_persona: Basketball is the big one, as it is for many Lithuanians. He watches Žalgiris games and EuroLeague streams late at night and follows the national team closely. He doesn't play any more. He walks a lot, usually long routes around Willen Lake or along the canal, mostly on his own with a podcast. He has a pull-up bar in the doorway and uses it most days.
card.arts_persona: Not much interested in galleries or theatre. He watches crime series and Scandinavian dramas with subtitles and listens to Lithuanian rock and some older Western stuff like Depeche Mode. He has read a few history books about the Soviet period and the Second World War.
card.travel_persona: Flies back to Lithuania once or twice a year from Luton, usually in summer and sometimes at Christmas, to see his mum and his older sister's family. He has been to Riga, Kraków and a cheap week in Tenerife with a friend. He books well in advance, compares prices obsessively and won't pay for extras he doesn't need.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks for himself most evenings, plain and filling: potatoes, pork, buckwheat, soups. He batch-cooks on his first day off and portions it into tubs for the week. He buys dark rye bread, kefir and smoked sausage from the Eastern European shop in Bletchley and does the rest at Aldi. He makes cepelinai only when his mum is visiting or when he's feeling homesick. He thinks English food is fine but overpriced in pubs.
hobbies_and_interests: Long solo walks around Milton Keynes lakes and the canal
Fixing and selling secondhand bikes and small electronics on Facebook Marketplace
Tracking his savings and spending in a spreadsheet
Fishing occasionally at a lake near Newport Pagnell
skills: Setting up and adjusting injection moulding machines
Basic mechanical repairs, bikes and household appliances
Speaks Lithuanian, fluent English, decent Russian
card.career_goals: Wants to move up to setter or shift technician, mainly for the money and so he doesn't have to deal with the worst of the line work. He is saving hard for a deposit on a small flat or house, either here or back in Lithuania; he hasn't fully decided which. He doesn't want to manage people.
card.voice: Fluent, practical English with a clear Lithuanian accent. He speaks in short sentences at a steady, unhurried pace. He sometimes drops 'the' or 'a' ('I go to shop after work') and occasionally puts words in a slightly unusual order, but he is easy to follow. He has picked up a few words from work and uses them naturally: 'mate', 'knackered', 'cheers', 'to be honest'. His filler is a flat 'eh' or 'mm' rather than 'erm', and he often answers 'yeah, yeah' quickly. He doesn't fill silences. If a question is vague he says 'What do you mean exactly?' rather than guessing. His answers are blunt and sometimes come across as dismissive.
card.typing: Short and functional. He usually capitalises the first word and stops there, with almost no full stops at the end. He often leaves out apostrophes ('dont', 'its'), uses commas sparingly and sometimes leaves out articles. He doesn't use emojis. A typical answer: 'Work shifts so weekdays not always possible, prefer evening'.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit cool at first. He is polite enough but doesn't do small talk and can come across as impatient or unfriendly. He answers exactly what's asked, keeps it brief and is a little suspicious of anyone who seems to want something from him. He warms up slightly if the conversation turns to something practical he knows about, or to money and prices, where he has strong opinions.
small_things: His shift pattern means he never knows what day of the week it is
The price of rent in Milton Keynes now compared to when he arrived
A bike he bought for twenty quid and sold for ninety
The Eastern European shop running out of the good rye bread
Neighbours below playing music too loud
deeper_things: Feels he has lived in England for sixteen years without really belonging to it, and that he doesn't fully belong back home any more either
His father drank heavily and died when Tomas was nineteen; part of why he left was to get away from that town
Still thinks about the relationship that ended, and admits he was too stubborn and controlling about money
Worries about his mother getting older on her own while he's a flight away
Sometimes wonders if all the saving is leading to anything
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot taken from slightly below at a desk, so the frame shows his head and shoulders and a bit of ceiling. He is lit mainly by the cool white glow of the screen plus a ceiling light behind him, which leaves his face a little flat and pale. He has a lean, angular face, light stubble, pale blue-grey eyes and a neutral, slightly guarded expression with his mouth closed. His short fair-brown hair is clippered at the sides, a bit longer on top and receding slightly at the temples. No glasses. He is wearing a plain dark grey hoodie with the zip half open over a black T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed photo of a lake with pine trees, a doorway with a black pull-up bar fitted across the top, and part of a neatly made bed with a navy duvet. A small clothes airer with a couple of work T-shirts and socks stands in the corner.
